title: WTO | Tariff and trade data
content:
WTO | Tariff and trade data WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION Home | About WTO | News & events | Trade topics | WTO membership | Documents & resources | External relations Contact us | Site map | A-Z | Search español français home trade topics tariffs get tariff data TARIFFS Tariff and trade data The WTO website offers many options for researching members' customs duty rates and their levels of exports/imports. The new WTO Tariff & Trade Data platform provides enhanced access to official tariff and trade figures for over 150 economies. It includes bilateral trade datasets, time series views, and reports on export
              and import patterns by product and trade partner. See also WTO Data Portal Trade Statistics Notification Data Economic research WTO Tariff and Trade Data Platform Through the WTO Tariff & Trade Data platform , users can obtain and compare
              two sets of customs tariffs: the legally bound commitments on customs duty rates, which act as ceilings on the tariffs that member governments can set and are known as "bound
                rates", with the rates that governments actually charge on imports, known as "applied rates" and which have a direct impact on trade. Recent tariff actions can
                also be consulted. The platform aggregates official information about applied tariffs and import data notified by WTO members to the WTO's Integrated Data Base (IDB), and bound duties
              (agreed maximum tariffs) and other commitments recorded in the WTO's Consolidated Tariff Schedules (CTS) database. This data is supplemented by the WTO Analytical
              Database (ADB), which integrates WTO sources such as regional trade agreements (RTA) and external partners such as the International Trade Centre (ITC), UN Comtrade
              and Trade Data Monitor. The platform follows a multi-tiered update schedule, with updates ranging from daily to monthly, depending on the data source. Integrated Database The Integrated Database (IDB) contains time series of the tariffs applied by WTO members and acceding economies to imports from other WTO members. Data are provided
              at the most detailed product level (usually the eight to ten digit product level or tariff line code). The database also contains import statistics, including the
              value and volume of imports by country of origin and by tariff line. Find out more Consolidated Tariff Schedules Database The Consolidated Tariff Schedules (CTS) Database contains the agreed maximum tariffs that WTO members can impose on imported products from other WTO members and, if
              applicable, their specific commitments in agriculture (domestic support, export subsidies and tariff quota information). Find out more WTO Analytical Database The WTO Analytical Database is a comprehensive tariff and trade flow database that consolidates most-favoured nation (MFN) bound, applied and preferential tariffs,
              together with trade flow data from various sources. These include Integrated Database (IDB) tariffs and import data, Consolidated Tariff Schedules (CTS) bound rates,
              preferential commitments from the WTO Regional Trade Agreements (RTA) Database, ITC data from the World Tariff Profile datasets as well as trade data from UN Comtrade
              and Trade Data Monitor (TDM). All data is standardized into time series at the Harmonized System subheading level. The result is a single, ready-to-query dataset showing — by product,
              partner and year — the legally bound duty, the MFN applied tariff, the preferential tariff a partner could claim, and the value of merchandise that crossed the
              border, all expressed in the same version of the HS. The data can be accessed through the WTO Tariff & Trade Data Platform . World Tariff Profiles The World Tariff Profiles is an annual co-publication by the World Trade Organization, the International Trade Centre, and the United Nations Conference on Trade and
              Development. This comprehensive statistical yearbook provides detailed information on tariffs and trade, as well as non-tariff measures. It covers over 170 countries
              and customs territories, including WTO members and non-WTO members for which the most recent tariff data is available. It is designed to facilitate comparisons across
              countries/territories, between various sectors, and specifically, to allow for comparison between bound and applied tariffs for WTO members. Find out more Customs codes and product categories Harmonized System Products in the databases are identified using the World Customs Organization's internationally agreed "Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System"
              (Harmonized System or HS). The HS codes are standard up to six digits, the most detailed level that can be compared internationally. Beyond that, WTO members are free to use their own
              definitions according to their individual requirements. The Harmonized System is regularly reviewed and amended. Detailed information on the evolution of the HS across its various editions can be found in https://hstracker.wto.org/ . Multilateral Trade Negotiation (MTN) product categories MTN categories are  key product grouping used by the WTO to classify goods, particularly in the "World Tariff Profiles". These categories encompass 22
              primary product groups, which are further subdivided into 72 sub-categories. The relationship between the six-digit HS codes and the WTO MTN product categories is
              available for download from the Tariff and Trade Data Platform. Find out more WTO member data Data are also available through each member's page on the WTO website (see, for example, Argentina ).
              These pages can be reached from the list of members . The original lists of members' bound commitments remain available. The digit-level of the bound duty rates in these “schedules of commitments” can vary
              from member to member. Share World Tariff Profiles Summary tables Publication Download pdf files for individual members Jargon buster ad valorem (AV) : a tariff rate charged as percentage of the price applied rates : duties that are actually charged on imports. These can be below the bound rates bound rates (tariff binding) : commitment not to increase a rate of duty beyond an agreed level. Once a rate of duty is bound, it may not be raised
                    without compensating the affected parties digits, digit-level : (tariffs) a reference to the codes used to identify products. Categories of products are subdivided by adding digits. See
                    Harmonized System Harmonized System : World Customs Organization’s system of code numbers for identifying products. The codes are standard up to six digits. Beyond
                    that countries can introduce national distinctions for tariffs and many other purposes MFN (most-favoured-nation) tariff : normal non-discriminatory tariff charged on imports (excludes preferential tariffs under free trade agreements and
                    other schemes or tariffs charged inside quotas) schedules : (for goods) list of bound tariff rates tariff line (TL in the tables) : a product, as defined by a system of code numbers for tariffs More jargon: glossary
